jurisdiction: County of Sonoma, CA — unincorporated area only (the nine cities are separate Authorities Having Jurisdiction and are outside this model)
implementer: Permit Sonoma (formerly the Permit and Resource Management Department, ordained by Sonoma County Ordinance 4906 in 1995) — Permit Intake plus six plan-check divisions: Building, Engineering, Well & Septic, Planning, Fire-referral review, Code Enforcement
process: Post-entitlement residential construction permit review under AB 2234 (2022): intake completeness determination, plan-check fee payment as clock trigger, multi-division plan check (serial → parallel), plan check comments and resubmittal, permit issuance, field inspection; plus the over-the-counter, express-permit, third-party plan check and self-certification alternative tracks, and the workflow-instrumentation layer that decides whether any of it can be measured.
scope_boundary: This is the county building-permit review machinery an ADU application runs through in unincorporated Sonoma County. It is NOT an ADU-specific process: the grand jury did not separate ADUs from other residential permits, and Permit Sonoma's AB 2234 clocks (15 business days completeness / 30 business days review for <25 units) are the general post-entitlement clocks, which run alongside — and are shorter than — the ADU-specific Gov. Code § 66317 clocks (15 business days completeness / 60 calendar days ministerial decision). A solver must not conflate the two clock sets. The report also explicitly excluded inspections and code enforcement from its scope.

Every quote in this file carries the OCR-corrected text in `quote` and, where correction was needed, the corresponding string from the saved .txt in `ocr_raw` plus a list of what was changed in `ocr_corrections`. CONVENTION: `ocr_raw` reproduces the .txt characters exactly except that line breaks and runs of whitespace are collapsed to single spaces; a hyphen at a line break therefore appears as '4- 8' where the .txt has '4-\n8'. Corrections are confined to obvious character-level scanning errors (l↔1, 6↔th, rn↔m, digit substitutions, dropped spaces). No wording, number or claim was inferred or reconstructed beyond that; where a number could not be recovered with confidence it is recorded as unrecoverable in known_gaps rather than guessed.

Whether PS published the OTC list (R4), the express-permit requirements (R5), the SOPs (R10) or the annual performance report (R12) is unknown — and if it did, several staff_only labels here would now be wrong.
notes:
Why Sonoma and not Santa Cruz: the brief asked for the richest county grand-jury report, and Sonoma wins on actor-by-actor sequence and on named clock-start events. Sonoma supplies the internal mechanism — Permit Intake as the single gateway, fee payment as the AB 2234 clock trigger, the serial→parallel plan-check change across six divisions, the Accela instrumentation gap sitting exactly on the statutory interval, the Access shadow database, the personal non-public checklists, and the Express Permit team. Santa Cruz's comparable report (corpus/realworld/_gold/raw/gj_santacruz_2025_permitting.txt) is richer in per-case narrative and has one excellent invisible dispatch rule (14 days on the aging report → send the file to an outside plan-check firm) but is weaker on sequence; it would make a good second county model.

Eleven of 29 activities are staff_only, the highest share of the four models in this batch, and they cluster in one place: the measurement layer. A05, A26 and A27 are the instrumentation; A10 and A11 are the interdepartmental coordination the instrumentation fails to capture; A13 and A19 are the criteria that were supposed to be published and are not; A20 and A22 are capacity mechanisms the applicant benefits from without knowing; A28 is the fee method; A29 is the reporting that closes the loop back to the Board with a figure the grand jury disputes. The instructive property for this project is that the hidden layer here is not a hidden *step* in the applicant's path — it is the absence of any reliable record of the path, which makes the statutory obligation formally unverifiable. Grand Jury Finding F3 states this outright. That is a different species of opacity from SF's held permits or San José's silent affordability imputation, and it is the reason this model is worth its OCR cost.

The single most transferable designed detail: the AB 2234 plan-check clock starts on PAYMENT of the plan check fee. Nothing in the statute says that. An applicant who does not know it cannot know when their own protection begins, and a solver reconstructing this process from declared sources would almost certainly start the clock at submittal or at acceptance.

gold_tier is 'designed+observed': the process model is designed-tier from interviews and document review, while the compliance rates (a handful of misses out of 7,000+ intakes; fewer than 20 of ~1,100 plan checks) come from the grand jury's own review of 50,000+ data records and 5,000+ task-status records.
